author: NorthEast News Desk
body: BRICS leaders unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on Saturday, expressing deep concern about the Middle East war and calling for maximum restraint. The formal adoption converts an earlier agreement among negotiators into the 10-member group’s official summit position.

The statement advocates a multilateral approach that respects national viewpoints and reiterates support for settling international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. Reaching consensus carried added significance because the expanded bloc includes both Iran and the United Arab Emirates, a close U.S. partner, while the United States and Iran have resumed exchanges of strikes after an August pause.

The declaration also raised concern about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort trade, against a backdrop of U.S. sanctions on Iran and Russia. BRICS now includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the UAE. The declaration provides a common diplomatic text, but implementation will depend on whether members can translate broad calls for restraint into coordinated action.
dek: The 10-member bloc urged maximum restraint and peaceful dispute resolution despite sharp differences among members over the conflict.
headline: BRICS unanimously adopts New Delhi declaration on Middle East war
